recipes.name: Black Bean Turkey Burgers
ingredients_raw: 1 cup black beans, rinsed and slightly crushed
1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Combine ground turkey, black beans, Parmesan cheese, bread crumbs, egg, and onion soup mix in a large bowl with your hands. Divide into 6 portions; shape into patties.
Cook on the preheated grill until no longer pink in centers, 5 to 6 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read at least 165 degrees F (75 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Black Bean Turkey Burgers
raw_recipe.description: This black bean turkey burger recipe uses Japanese-style panko bread crumbs, egg, Parmesan cheese, and black beans to help hold their form on the grill.

review.reviewBody: I got 6 large burgers out of this and they were so delicious! I find that oftentimes when I make turkey burgers they come out too dry but I think that adding the beans gave them some much-needed moisture. I used 1.3 lbs turkey, a whole can of black beans (drained and rinsed), a bit more than a half cup of the Panko breadcrumbs, skipped the Parmesan cheese and the soup mix and used some onion powder, garlic powder, cumin, and cayenne pepper instead. Yum!!! I can't wait to make these again!

The kids and I loved these. I did modify just a bit to meet my dietary needs. I added a handful of spinach to the food processor when I processed the black beans. I did not use bread crumbs, used a 1/2 cup of mexican shredded cheese instead. I also seasoned with Montreal steak seasoning and a tbs of onion powder. Cooked them on the George Forman and OMG they were GOOD!!!!!
I ADDED 1 1/2 CUPS OF BLACK BEANS AND CHOPPED THEM VERY FINE. THE FAMILY LOVED THEM...!!!

So good and easy. I baked in the oven at 350 F for 20 minutes instead of grilling, and they turned out great. Also added a bit of cayenne pepper as some said that it was too bland. This recipe was in the magazine. They included a garlicky aioli which I made. It really made the burger! Garlicky aioli: Stir together 3/4 cup mayonnaise, 2 Tbsp lemon juice, 1 Tbsp minced garlic, 3/4 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Even the kids liked these! I browned mine in a pan and baked at 375 for 15 minutes. Also, I ran out of onion soup packets so I substituted with a ranch dressing packet. Yummy!
These burgers were really good. I did not do the bread crumbs or soup mix. I did about 1 1/2 TBSP onion powder, and baked it on 375 for 25 minutes.

I'm giving 4 stars because I made substitutions and didn't follow the exact recipe. We are in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic (wasn't going to run to store for items) I did not have bread crumbs, the soup mix and cheese so those were left out.
I added chopped onion, garlic powder, cumin, chili flakes, and cayenne powder to taste. 
I used 1.5 lbs of turkey and a whole can of black beans and 1 egg.
I followed another review and cooked patties on a stone in the oven at 350 for 30 min. 
Burgers were delish and juicy. My family loved them. We topped our burgers with mushrooms, avocado, spring mix and bacon on an onion bun. We will definitely make again - next time hopefully I will have the panko and other ingredients.

This was excellent! I followed the recipe, except for using some spices instead of the onion soup mix I didn't have. Very moist and great flavor! I sauteed some onion to have on top. I grilled them on top of some foil for the first side, since the mixture was so soft and moist, then I took them off the foil for the 2nd side.

This was so very tasty. I used a whole can of beans and used the food processor to slightly chop them as another person suggested. I omitted the cheese because I don't like cheese. I fried the burgers, using very little oil, because I thought they would fall apart on the grill. The recipe using a whole can of beans made 6 large burgers. They were so good they didn't need ketsup or mustard. I will definitely make these burgers again.

My husband and I thought these were delicious. I was out of onion soup mix, so I googled a recipe for it using pantry spices, and made my own. I was able to form 6 nice size patties out of this recipe, and I cooked them on a grill pan on the stove. Had Potato Rolls & Coleslaw with the Turkey Burgers, for the win. Great weeknight meal! :)

HOLY COW, these are amazing!!!! I made some additions to the seasoning that I'd highly recommend:
*Added cumin, cayenne and sriracha. Oh, and smoked paprika!!! Yummm.
*I substituted Mexican shredded cheese for parmesan because that's what I had. (I know, totally not the same thing, but I'm job hunting at the moment, sooo...)
*Instead of grilling them, I put them in the oven on a wavy griddle rack thingy at 375 for about 35 minutes. I had some mixture left over, so I did a couple in the frying pan and was able to compare them. They were both good, but the oven ones were incredibly crispy on the outside. Seriously, seriously delicious. Oh, and I flipped them about 10 minutes before taking them out. I froze some too, and they reheated like a champ.

Seriously, try these. How many recipes do you know that are a) cheap, b) low fat, c) pretty quick to make, and d) brain-meltingly delicious?

This recipe was soooo good and super easy to make. I'm always happy to discover something new that I love. I will definitely make this again. The only thing I changed was to put sharp cheddar on top of the burgers. I did try goat cheese as suggested in the recipe but I don't think it works as well as the cheddar.
I used sauteed onions and fresh garlic and herbs, spices instead of onion mix. Delicious May never make plain turkey burgers again.
Just okay as written. Not bad, but came out a bit mushy and somewhat bland.
This is my ultimate go to recipe for a burger. I use chopped onions in place of dry onion mix.

I tried this recipe and my family loved it. It is probably the best Turkey Burger I've ever had. It's super moist (not dry because of the turkey meat) and it's very savory. 10 out of 10, yes I recommend.

I used 99% fat free turkey and the beans were perfect to keep it moist. I had everything on hand except for the onion soup mix, so I added a mixture of dried onion and Mediterranean seasoning and so good. Topped with tomato, red onion, pickles and avocado on a toasted bagel. So good!
Used entire can of black beans, substituted Italian cheese blend for parm, and cooked on George Foreman grill. Served with tomato, spinach, avocado and sriracha mayo. Really turned out well.

This was a great first try at making a non-beef patty. I used Italian breadcrumbs instead of Panko, and also added cilantro. I did six minutes on each side and they came out perfect. I also put a little Sriracha on them when eating to give it a little spice. I thought they were delicious!
These were fantastic! Due to product on hand - one can of blackbeans, seasoned breadcrumbs. Rest the same :)
